data.name: M_WitnessModeNotice
data.value: Ordinary mode draws locally immediately, works offline, and saves a locally replayable proof. When online, new proofs are submitted for server replay verification in the background and a third-party time stamp is requested (the proof digest only — never the roster or draw content). Historical proofs are not uploaded automatically; you can upload them manually on the verification website. Proofs form an append-only hash chain, so later edits, deleted proofs, and a wiped-and-rebuilt chain are all detectable, and each proof commits a digest of the record-id-to-name mapping of the roster it used, so editing the list afterwards is detectable too. It does not prove that the local program, random seed, or roster was unchanged before the draw, nor rule out filtering the roster before drawing.

data.name: M_ModeConfirmLocal
data.value:
Ordinary mode draws locally immediately, works offline, and saves a replayable proof. When online, the app submits one replay-signing request to fair.sectl.cn in the background only for each newly completed ordinary draw and requests a third-party time stamp (the proof digest only — never the roster or draw content). Offline or failed historical proofs are not uploaded automatically.
Proofs form an append-only hash chain, so later edits, deleted proofs, and a wiped-and-rebuilt chain are detectable; the service also remembers the chain head it has seen for each device, so rebuilding after deleting the local proofs is reported as a backwards chain position.
Each proof commits a digest of the "record id to name/number/group" mapping of the roster it used, so editing the list afterwards to point a winning record at someone else is detectable.
It cannot prove that the local program, real roster, or random seed was unchanged before the draw, nor rule out repeated trials and selection before the draw, or filtering the roster before drawing.

data.name: M_ModeConfirmFormal
data.value:
The following is SecRandom's (upstream project's) description, with minor punctuation adjustments and annotations
"Formal notarization" first locks this anonymous candidate pool, weights, and rules at fair.sectl.cn; the server then generates random material, calculates the final result, and stores an "immutable official proof" (here referring to SECTL, the unincorporated organization that controls this product's upstream project)
If network instability, disconnection, service unavailability, device failure, or force majeure prevents a completed server proof, this "formal notarization" produces no local substitute result and does not fall back to ordinary mode. After the server confirms the lock, the candidate pool, weights, rules, random material, and result cannot be replaced, supplemented, or recalculated in the same flow; any new draw can only be a separate, independent "notarization"
It prevents replacement of local draw code, random seeds, or result files during the locked flow, but it still cannot prove that the real roster is complete and authentic, or that the candidate pool was not manually filtered before submission

data.name: M_ModeConfirmFormalNotice
data.value: This feature is provided by upstream SecRandom, which named it "formal notarization"; that name is upstream's own description of its feature and does not mean VeriRandom evaluates its legal nature or effect. Using this feature submits data to SECTL servers under SecRandom's terms of service and privacy policy. For the feature's exact mechanism and effect, rely on SECTL's official documentation. In this build, the mechanism included in this feature treats the SecRandom central server as its "sole trust" root; qualifying wording such as "sole" is an objective technical description and does not constitute an express or implied evaluation

data.name: M_ModeConfirmFormalWarning
data.value: Before relying on this feature as evidence that must have legal effect, strictly confirm whether it actually meets your requirements

data.name: S_TimestampAuthority_D
data.value: On by default; every proof requests an RFC 3161 time stamp from the WoTrus TSA and only the proof digest is sent. Turning it off stops time stamping, and beacon matching then loses its period anchor and can only go back to the pulse through the index recorded in the reference proof

data.name: C_TimestampDisableBody
data.value: Without time stamps a proof has no anchor that is independent of the SecRandom service. Beacon verification also loses its period anchor: it can still fetch the pulse by the index recorded in the reference proof, but it can no longer match that pulse against the period the proof was stamped in, including the previous period inside the tolerance. Turn this off only if you understand both effects

data.name: C_TimestampDisableConfirm
data.value: I understand and still want to turn it off

data.value: The time stamp is more than 60 seconds after its beacon pulse (previous period), so the score is halved

data.name: S_BeaconEntropy_D
data.value: When on, ordinary mode derives its draw seed from a NIST beacon pulse so the operator cannot inject custom entropy; each pulse assigns sequence numbers starting at 0 and increasing by 1, so no sequence repeats within a pulse; an unavailable beacon fails the draw instead of falling back to a local seed; ordinary mode only

data.name: S_BeaconEndpoint_D
data.value: Defaults to the official NIST Beacon v2 endpoint; with a mirror the proof still records the pulse value and signature so the pulse can be checked against the authority afterwards; remote endpoints must use HTTPS
